claims.claim_text: George Ciampa has a high-confidence identifier-backed Army record match.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an Army private entry dated 7 February 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name plus exact private identifier in an official Army record; assessed high confidence pending the personnel-file bridge to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army entry establishes a wartime observation but not the date or route of later OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Occupation value 999 has no defensible label in the inspected code pages and is not decoded. A famous George W Ciampa veteran has a different identifier and later entry date and was rejected as a namesake.

claims.claim_text: Clement Cianfichi has a high-confidence match to the documented Army OSS veteran of that distinctive name.
claims.evidence_excerpt: served the USA in the Army as a member of the 'Office of Strategic Service' in Europe during WWII
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary identifies the exact distinctive name as a Hibbing-born Army OSS veteran in Europe and a demolition specialist.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Distinctive exact full name and direct Army OSS context support high confidence; the index identifier is absent from the incomplete Army merged file, so the match is not called confirmed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary places the individual in Army OSS service during World War II but does not establish entry chronology or pre-service work.
claims.match_notes: The obituary's post-1959 carpentry career is not projected backward as a pre-OSS occupation or employer. Absence from the Army merged file is not negative proof.

claims.claim_text: Guy A Ciaraldi has a high-confidence identifier-backed Army record match with an unresolved chronology.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact indexed name and private identifier match a master-sergeant Army entry dated 1 July 1946, after OSS termination.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name plus exact private identifier supports high-confidence identity, but it does not explain the relationship between the 1946 Army event and the earlier OSS index entry.
claims.temporal_assessment: The entry date is after NARA's documented 20 September 1945 OSS termination date, so the record cannot establish a pre-OSS occupation or immediate assignment.
claims.match_notes: Occupation value 177 is not assigned a label in the inspected official summary. It is not decoded, and the post-dissolution Army row is routed to temporal review.

claims.claim_text: Arthur Ciarmicoli has a high-confidence match to the United States Army sergeant documented with the Chrysler Mission.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Captain Victor Giannino, Sergeant Arthur Ciarmicoli and Sergeant LoDolce
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1952 federal court decision identifies Sergeant Arthur Ciarmicoli as a United States Army member of the Chrysler Mission in northern Italy in October 1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive exact name and documented wartime Army mission align with the OSS index; no contradictory same-name candidate was found. No private identifier is available, so the match is high confidence rather than confirmed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The court decision establishes an October 1944 Army assignment but does not establish the route into OSS or any pre-service employment.
claims.match_notes: The Army mission evidence supports enlisted status and identity only. It is not presented as an immediate pre-OSS affiliation or a civilian employer.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an official Army private entry dated 7 February 1942. The row's occupation value 999 is not assigned a defensible label in the inspected official pages; the famous George W Ciampa veteran has a different identifier and 1943 entry chronology and is rejected as a namesake.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 and the original Army card to establish George Ciampa's occupation, named employer, work dates and Army-to-OSS chronology without relying on the unrelated famous veteran.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The distinctive exact name and direct Army OSS context in a reputable obituary identify Clement Cianfichi as a Hibbing-born veteran who served with OSS in Europe. His private index identifier is absent from the incomplete Army merged file, so identity remains high confidence rather than confirmed.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Clement Cianfichi's service identifier, unit and pre-Army occupation or employer; do not project his post-1959 master-carpenter career backward.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an official Army master-sergeant entry dated 1 July 1946. Because that date follows OSS termination on 20 September 1945, the row supports identity and enlisted status but not a pre-OSS occupation or pathway; value 177 is not decoded.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 and the original Army card to explain the post-OSS 1946 entry event, establish earlier service chronology and locate a named pre-OSS affiliation or employer.
